title: Summer Camp Management System
summary: Relational database for a summer camp: 14 MySQL tables, business rules, and four analytical queries; integrate enrollment, payment, logistics, staffing, etc.

outcomes.name: Computed 324 camper beds and 88 staff beds across active cabins
Answered four management questions with one SQL query each
Linked 14 tables and documented 10 business rules

artifacts.notes: Zip copy was 0 bytes; this is the re-attached 27-page PDF.

problem: Camp records live in separate systems for staff, campers, payroll, health, and logistics, which makes it hard to see the whole operation or compare it year to year.
approach: Designed and built a 14-table relational database in MySQL with documented business rules. Loaded it from CSV and wrote queries that answer real management questions.
limitations: Built and tested on sample data. The report labels all figures as examples of how the database could operate and handle situations.

title: Predicting Job Callbacks Using Resume Data
summary: Statistically sound ML study of which resume features relate to interview callbacks, using a synthetic dataset.

outcomes.name: Random forest predicts callbacks at 70.5% accuracy
Education and professional level are significantly associated with callbacks
Logistic regression baseline reaches 66.7% accuracy

problem: Which resume features are linked to interview callbacks, and can a model predict them reliably?
approach: Team project of three. Cleaned the data with rule-based checks, ran chi-square and correlation tests, and compared logistic regression with random forest models.
limitations: The dataset and labels are synthetic, so the results show the method, not real hiring practice.

figures.caption: Mean callback rate by education level

headline: A random forest model predicts interview callbacks at 70.5% accuracy, above a 66.7% baseline, and finds education and professional level significantly linked to callbacks.

title: Visualizing International Science and Engineering Fair Trends (2014–2024)
summary: Cleans and analyzes ISEF award data to find trends in categories, awards, and keywords across a decade.

outcomes.name: Audited ISEF records and quantified missing category data
Analyzed 14,873 ISEF projects across 2014–2024

problem: What do ISEF competition records from 2014 to 2024 show about trends in categories and awards, and how reliable is the data?
approach: Cleaned and deduplicated 14,873 project records, audited missing data year by year, and analyzed category trends and keywords in Python.
limitations: About 20% of records lack category values in some years, which limits year-to-year comparisons.

figures.caption: Hypothesis test: does category growth predict award win rate?

headline: Audit found 68.4% of 2015 and 82.3% of 2016 ISEF records lack category data, so trends for those years are unreliable until cleaned.

title: Modeling Life Expectancy and Country Development Indicators
summary: Models how BMI, immunization, schooling, and GDP relate to life expectancy and development status.

outcomes.name: Development indicators explain 61.1% of variation in life expectancy
A classification model reaches 94.2% overall accuracy

artifacts.notes: Prefix says 'Live', project is 'Life'. Linked by suffix; confirm and rename.

problem: Which development indicators, such as BMI, immunization, schooling, and GDP, are linked to life expectancy?
approach: Compared t-tests, correlation tests, linear and generalized models, random forest, and a support vector machine in R, and evaluated each model.
limitations: The report notes that some classification accuracy may be inflated.

figures.caption: Ten-year change in life expectancy, developed vs. developing countries (2002–2012)
Average life expectancy by region over time

headline: BMI, immunization, schooling, and GDP together explain 61.1% of the variation in life expectancy, a practical guide for public health and development planning.

title: Investigating Divergence and Adaptations Between Heat Shock Proteins of Thermophilic Prokaryotes and Mesophilic Eukaryotes
summary: Comparative sequence analysis and phylogenetics of heat shock proteins across thermophilic and mesophilic organisms.

outcomes.name: Thermophilic prokaryotes have significantly higher median GC content
Two components explain 50.1% of variance in HSP sequence features
Average percent identity of 24.5% across divergent HSP sequences

problem: How do heat shock proteins differ between thermophilic prokaryotes and mesophilic eukaryotes?
approach: Aligned sequences in R with Bioconductor, built phylogenetic trees, applied principal component analysis, and tested GC content differences.
limitations: Some tree branches have low bootstrap confidence (39% in one case), so the tree structure is tentative.

figures.caption: Principal component analysis of sequence distances

headline: Heat shock proteins in thermophilic prokaryotes have significantly higher GC content, and two sequence patterns explain half of their variation (50.1%).

title: Determining Bone Health Utilizing Visible Light
summary: Arduino-based visible-light device that tests bone porosity as a screening signal for osteoporosis.
business_context: Health screening and medical device R&D

outcomes.name: Light-sensor resistance rises after boiling, separating porous from dense samples
Built and tested a visible-light prototype

problem: Porous bone raises fracture risk in osteoporosis. Can visible light reveal differences in bone porosity?
approach: Built an Arduino device with a light-dependent resistor and measured resistance before and after boiling bone samples, which changes porosity.
limitations: Tested on bovine bone samples, not human bone.

title: Leadership Transfers!: Transfer Ambassador Program Proposal
summary: Proposal for a 4-week leadership development course for transfer students as a Spring community and campus resource, complete with campus partners, activities, outcomes, and risk mitigation.
business_context: Transfer student engagement and leadership development at a large public university

outcomes.name: Structured proposal and SWOT analysis for 3 programs, each with 4 sessions
Four sessions: involvement, time management and systems, influence and team building, and career stories

problem: Transfer students have less time than other students to get involved and grow into campus leadership roles. Most leadership programs serve students already in leadership or underclassmen, and campus leadership offerings are not adequately advertised or coordinated.
approach:
**Analyzed** outcomes from previous programs and gaps in programming to identify opportunities and guidelines for successful programs.
**Proposed** three Spring programs for the Transfer Center, each with four sessions.
**Wrote** a four-week leadership course with five campus partners. Students build skills through workshops on involvement, time management and systems, influence and team building, and turning involvement into a career story.
**Planned** each program's opportunities, potential issues, a plan to counteract those issues, and each event.
limitations: This work is currently a proposal and is waiting on department approval for deployment in Spring 2027. It demonstrates my ability to understand user needs, evaluate outcomes from previous programs to shape future activities, design clear programs with purpose and activities, identify opportunities, identify and manage risks and issues, develop comprehensive programs, and communicate professionally.
headline: Structured proposal and SWOT analysis for 4-week leadership course with 5 campus partners.
